findings.question: q-biology-botany-0006
findings.quote: Phloem conducting cells remain alive and work with companion cells.
findings.problem: This assigns companion cells to phloem without restricting the statement to flowering plants. As the lesson explains, conifers and ferns have different helper cells, not companion cells. The stem does not specify a flowering plant.
findings.fix: Say that phloem conducting cells remain alive; specify that they work with companion cells in flowering plants.

findings.question: q-biology-botany-0012
findings.quote: No; root responses to light vary.
findings.problem: The key is the only qualified choice. All three distractors use conspicuous absolutes: every organ must respond identically, every root must always grow away, or roots are completely unable to respond. A student can select the cautious statement by choice form without knowing root responses to light.
findings.fix: Use plausible, similarly qualified alternatives so that the student must understand organ-specific light responses.
